riskAssessment.rationale: The page tells small-business owners which retirement plan to adopt and states IRS tax rules (a 25% additional tax, rollover taxation, eligibility, one-plan rule). Those are consequential financial/legal-tax claims, so HIGH. Specific misstatements found are listed as F1 to F10.

consequentialClaims.quote: A 401(k) also allows penalty-free withdrawals if you leave your employer at age 55 or older, an exception that does not apply to a SIMPLE IRA.
consequentialClaims.reason: Misstates when the age-55 exception applies and implies no tax at all; a reader could take a taxable withdrawal as free of tax.

consequentialClaims.quote: If business growth pushes your headcount past 100 qualifying workers, the IRS provides a two-year grace period to maintain the plan or transition to another option.
consequentialClaims.reason: Misstates the IRS grace period rule that decides whether an employer may keep its SIMPLE IRA.

consequentialClaims.quote: The IRS treats any rollover to a 401(k) or a Traditional IRA during this period as an early distribution, which triggers ordinary income tax and the full 25% penalty.
consequentialClaims.reason: Omits the IRS condition 'unless you qualify for an exception' on a 25% tax outcome.

incidentalMentions.quote: The IRS treats SIMPLE IRAs as an exclusive plan
incidentalMentions.reason: Inherited FAQ wording flagged by the keyword classifier ('treats'); it describes the one-plan rule and is reviewed under F8.
